They say he did well enough to own a little trading house somewhere in Baileste. // So he comes struttin' into this town to make that house bigger, only his wife runs off with the kids and his whole fortune, // and when he hears that, he loses all will to go home and he's been squattin' here ever since... that's about the size of it. // Plenty of folks get this wrong, pal: a merchant don't succeed by bein' good with numbers. Least of all a trader. // Land or sea, it's danger all the way, and a safe route don't pay. Spot a rival house's ship, ya attack it and sink the cargo. // Ya cheat folks, ya knock down your rivals, and even then there's no tellin' if the goods'll really sell. // Haul it all that way, and if the town's glutted with the stuff, the whole voyage is a dead loss. A gamblin' trade with no guarantees at all... that's traders for ya. // So take that old geezer for some bean counter and get cocky, and you'll get hurt. // Especially since that geezer's got no brains, so watch out. Brainless types'll pull a sword without it makin' a lick of sense.
